# Forward-query physical near-optimal recovery for arbitrary low-support channels

2026-10-29. Root extension prompted by the mixed-encoder construction; independent review pending. This removes the perfect-correctability premise, not the low-support/memoryless/trusted-control premises.

## Factorization without an accessible purification
Let N:L(C^k)->L(C^D) be any memoryless CPTP map and suppose rank N(I_k/k)<=d, with d<=D a supplied upper bound. Let V:C^d->C^D be any isometry extending the support of N(I/k). Every output of N lies in this support: for positive rho, rho<=k(I/k) implies N(rho)<=kN(I/k), and linearity extends the support statement to every operator. Thus F(X)=V†N(X)V is a CPTP channel k->d and N=V F. Neither V nor F is supplied to the controller.

If N has Kraus rank s, then the output support is contained in the span of the s Kraus images, so d<=ks suffices (or d=D when smaller). This is an upper-bound promise, not a learned Kraus decomposition. The channel may lose logical information irreversibly. No exact error-correcting code or perfectly recoverable subsystem is assumed.

## Reuse of the physical construction
Jointly compress N training Choi outputs and the later payload using the established reference-safe compression channel. The resulting state is the single-common-U ensemble of training and payload from A_U=U F, U Haar in U(d). This is again a channel identity with all logical references retained, so conditional on U the training experiments are IID and independent of the unknown payload. Apply the same finite tomography, rational TP/positive repair and actual synthesized Petz map from the received base theorem.

Write
 F_opt(N)=sup_R F_e(I_k/k,R N),
where R ranges over all CPTP physical decoders D->k. This optimum is unchanged by replacing N with F or U F: a decoder can be restricted through V, and a small-space decoder can be extended to all of D by a support measurement plus fixed output on its orthogonal complement. This is an existence comparison, not access to the unknown support projection.

On the good tomography event let halfdiamond(Ahat,A_U)<=delta. The unknown optimal recovery for A_U has fidelity on Ahat at least max(0,F_opt-delta). Barnum--Knill gives the learned physical Petz map fidelity on Ahat at least max(0,F_opt-delta)^2. Returning to the actual A_U loses at mostdelta. For0<=delta<=1,

**ACCEPT the squared-entanglement-fidelity near-optimal recovery theorem at the stated memoryless, low-output-support, coherent-training scope.** Perfect correctability and the mixed-isometry structure are not needed for this extension. The corrected finite tomography/physical-Petz construction and reference-joint compression/compiler receipts remain load-bearing dependencies.

The accepted statement is

`F_e(I_k/k, M_N) >= F_opt(N)^2 - 3delta - beta - gamma`,

where M_N is the entire one-payload recovered channel, including its fresh training queries, joint compression, measurement/feedforward and physical recovery. This is not diamond-near-optimality, approximation of the true source's Petz map, or an unconditional guarantee of recovery close to identity.

## 1. Support factorization is a complete channel identity

Let `S=N(I_k/k)` and P be its support projector. For every input density matrix rho, `rho<=I_k`, hence `N(rho)<=k S` and its output is supported on P. For an arbitrary positive unnormalized input, the same argument uses the additional trace factor. An equivalent direct Kraus proof is stronger in presentation: `S=(1/k)sum_l K_l K_l†` implies `(I-P)K_l=0` for every l. Thus **all** channel Kraus images lie in the support, including for entangled/reference inputs.

Choose any isometry V from C^d into C^D whose image contains P, padding the support when needed. Then `F(X)=V† N(X)V` is CP and trace preserving, and `N=Ad(V) composed with F` as a linear channel identity. Neither V nor F must be accessible to the controller. If a Kraus-rank upper bound s is supplied, one may choose `d=min(D,ks)` because the union of s Kraus images has dimension at most ks. This is the precise reading of the source's shorthand: not every smaller d is automatically a valid support bound.

# Standard known-channel SDP bridge to additive-optimal opaque recovery
2026-10-29. Author theorem, receiving review pending. The optimization method is conventional, not a new SDP or new QEC criterion.

## Known finite optimization problem
Let C:k->d be the rational CPTP channel reconstructed in the accepted compressed-channel learner. Let its normalized Choi state use input-first tensor order. In column-vectorized recovery order (output k fastest), define
 W=(S C^T S†)/k,
where S permutes the Choi factors into that recovery ordering. Equivalently W=sum_l vec(K_l†)vec(K_l†)†/k² for ANY Kraus representation of C. This identity is representation independent and the matrix is computed directly from rational C, without extracting unknown source Kraus operators. W>=0, TrW=1/k, ||W||op<=1/k.

For recovery Choi J=sum_a vec(L_a)vec(L_a)†, entanglement fidelity is Tr(WJ), and its exact primal/dual SDPs are
 max Tr(WJ), J>=0, Tr_output_k J=I_d;
 min TrY, Y Hermitian, Y tensor I_k>=W.
The primal center J0=I_(kd)/k is strictly feasible, has smallest eigenvalue1/k and trace d. Feasible primal matrices have trace d and Frobenius norm<=d. The dual has strictly feasible Y=(1+1/k)I_d. Strong duality holds and the common optimum is F_opt(C). This is the standard optimum-recovery SDP of Fletcher–Shor–Win (quant-ph/0606035v1, SecIV), applied to a learned small channel rather than a supplied original ambient channel.

## Finite weak-SDP contract and exact repairs
For target0<zeta<1, set xi=zeta/(16d). Use a conventional rational weak-SDP algorithm to obtain rational Hermitian J,Y with
 Tr_output J=I_d EXACTLY,
 J>=-xi I,
 Y tensor I_k-W>=-xi I,
 TrY-Tr(WJ)<=zeta/4.
All inequalities are required certified conditions, not a floating solver stopping message. Exact affine TP is imposed by rational linear parameterization; PSD slack can be certified using rational matrix separation/eigenvalue enclosures. A proposed numerical solution which fails the checks is not accepted.

Repair by
